newsitem.title: USA: Jury to decide punishment in trial of Texas mother.
newsitem.headline: Jury to decide punishment in trial of Texas mother.

text.p: Witnesses testified Monday that a Texas woman convicted on one count of capital murder in the stabbing death of her two sons was an indifferent, at times abusive, mother who gave drugs and liquor to her babysitter.
But family members described Darlie Routier, 27, as a loving mother who could not have killed sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, and pleaded with the jury not to sentence her to death.
The testimony was part of the trial's punishment phase in which the jury will decide if Routier gets the death penalty or goes to jail. Deliberations were expected to begin on Tuesday.

Routier on Saturday was found guilty of capital murder for stabbing to death son Damon while he and brother Devon slept June 6 in their Rowlett, Texas,home near Dallas. A second capital murder charge is pending in the death of Devon but prosecutors have not said if they will pursue it.
Capital murder is a more serious charge than murder and carries with it the possibility of a death sentence. All capital murder convictions are automatically appealed under Texas law.

Prosecutors said Routier killed in a fit of rage about family financial difficulties and her ongoing weight problems. She testified the children were murdered by a knife-wielding intruder who also attacked her.
Prosecutors said they would ask that Routier be put to death by lethal injection.
A Routier acquaintance, 18-year-old Allison Hennessey, testified Monday that Routier gave marijuana, liquor and cigarettes to a babysitter she and her husband Darin routinely used on weekends.

"She was an adult giving my best friend (the babysitter) things I don't agree with," Hennessey said. She and other witnesses also said the Routier boys often played outside without proper supervision.

A neighbour, Eileen Schirmer, told the jury she once saw Routier grab Devon by the back of his head and smash cake in his face when he sprayed water on her at his birthday party. "She said he was warned and got what he deserved," Schirmer said.
But Darlie Kee, Routier's mother, told the jury her daughter was "a very kind and sweet person" who was such a good mother that "she taught me to be a better grandmother.
"From June 6 on, this family has endured hell on Earth...I ask you, if you have any compassion, do not put her to death because she did not do this," Kee said.
A spokesman for the Texas Department of Corrections said Texas has six women on death row.
